title: UI: Allow direct kb/mouse actions on zoom tool button
body:
## What I did

Supports https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/pull/33375.

I allowed for more direct keyboard and scroll operation, directly on the button. This helps keyboard users who expect ArrowDown to do something on other toolbar tools with a popup, and provides a more direct shortcut for mouse users (scroll the zoom button) that is commonly found in graphics apps with a canvas and zoom controls.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`@testing-library user-event wheel scroll event support`

💡 Result:

Short answer: @testing-library/user-event does not expose a dedicated wheel/scroll helper. Use DOM fireEvent / createEvent to dispatch a WheelEvent (or construct new WheelEvent) and trigger scroll handlers. See the Testing Library fireEvent docs and the WheelEvent spec for event properties. [1][2]

References
- fireEvent / createEvent (DOM Testing Library). [1]
- WheelEvent (MDN). [2]

---

🌐 Web query:

`Storybook userEvent API wheel events documentation`

💡 Result:

Short answer: Storybook re-exports Testing Library’s userEvent for play() functions, but there’s no documented userEvent.wheel helper — use fireEvent.wheel or synthesize a WheelEvent instead.

Example:
- using fireEvent:
  await fireEvent.wheel(element, { deltaY: 100 });  // simulate vertical wheel
- or native:
  element.dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent('wheel', { deltaY: 100 }));

Sources:
[1] Storybook — Interaction tests / userEvent docs.  
[2] Testing Library — user-event intro (v14).  
[3] Testing Library — fireEvent / firing events docs.  
[4] MDN — WheelEvent (constructor & deltaY).

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Use the zoom control’s actual role consistently in these play functions.**

These stories query `"button"` for `"Change zoom level"`, while this file’s own helper (`openDialog`) targets it as `"switch"`. This can break interaction lookup/assertions.



<details>
<summary>🔧 Proposed fix pattern (apply to all new keyboard/wheel stories)</summary>

```diff
-const zoom = await canvas.findByRole('button', { name: 'Change zoom level' });
+const zoom = await canvas.findByRole('switch', { name: 'Change zoom level' });

-expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Change zoom level' })).toHaveTextContent('101%');
+expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Change zoom level' })).toHaveTextContent('101%');
```

```diff
-await waitFor(() =>
-  expect(screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Change zoom level' })).toHaveTextContent('150%')
-);
+await waitFor(() =>
+  expect(canvas.getByRole('switch', { name: 'Change zoom level' })).toHaveTextContent('150%')
+);
```
</details>


Also applies to: 99-103, 109-113, 119-123, 129-133, 139-143, 149-153, 160-164

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/manager/components/preview/tools/zoom.stories.tsx` around lines
89 - 93, The tests use findByRole('button', { name: 'Change zoom level' }) but
the component's helper openDialog and the actual control use role 'switch',
causing lookup failures; update the play functions that query the zoom control
(e.g., where you assign const zoom = await canvas.findByRole(...)) to use
findByRole('switch', { name: 'Change zoom level' }) consistently (same change
for all occurrences noted around the zoom keyboard/wheel stories), keep the
subsequent zoom.focus(), userEvent.keyboard/wheel calls and assertions unchanged
other than the role string so the interactions target the real control.
```

</details>
